subject: ENG
course_description: Exploration of the ways in which literary writers have developed scientific ideas and scientists have expressed themselves through creative writing.
course_notes: How do medical breakthroughs spark literary innovation, and how does literature, in turn, reshape medicine? Through case studies spanning tuberculosis, hysteria, cancer, and the shift from miasma to germ theory, students will explore the historical dialogue between the life sciences and the literary imagination. Together, we will examine how medical models rely on cultural narratives to make sense of new scientific discoveries, and how imaginative writing has amplified, challenges, and transformed clinical practices. In addition to literary writing, we will engage with medical primary source texts, as well as recent critical and theoretical writing, providing students with a deeper understanding of how the stories we tell about the body actively shape medical knowledge. Course Tags: Pre-1900 and Theories and Methods
